prompt:
Use case: historical-scene / identity-preserve character reference composition. Generate ONE NEW highly detailed photorealistic wide landscape image, 16:9, highest available resolution, requested 3840x2160. A user-directed imaginative Ahom royal festival scene at a NEW CLEAN Kareng Ghar, Garhgaon. This combines project character designs intentionally; it is not a documented historical gathering. No text or labels anywhere.

REFERENCE ROLES, EXACT:
Image 1 Suteuphaa character sheet: preserve his EXACT individual face, short black hair, strong brows, gold ribbed rounded cap with white feather, blue knee-length coat with gold collar/placket/cuffs, mustard-gold trousers, burgundy sash and sheathed sword. Depict this man ONCE, seated as Swargadeu.
Image 2 Ambika: preserve exact individual face, low black bun, cream fitted long-sleeved silk upper garment, cream wrap with purple woven borders/tassels, long gold earrings and bangles. Depict her ONCE.
Image 3 Sarbeswari: preserve exact distinct face, ornate twin round gold-and-red headdress, golden blouse, white shoulder drape, white lower wrap with red diamond woven motifs, purple waist sash, gold and red-bead jewellery. Depict her ONCE.
Image 4 Nasoni sheet: match this woman's face on ONE featured nasoni, and use her costume for a small group of THREE female Bihu dancers: red long-sleeved blouse, cream silk mekhela and separate sador with red woven borders, floral bun, traditional gold ornaments. Give the other two different faces.
Image 5 Dhulia sheet: match this young man's face on ONE featured drummer; a SECOND dhulia has a different face. Both wear cream short-sleeved shirt with red woven decoration, white dhoti, red-white headband, waist gamosa, large correctly shaped double-headed wooden Bihu dhol suspended horizontally across waist by a shoulder strap. They are WATCHING rather than dancing.
Image 6 earlier generated palace: use overall Kareng Ghar geometry only.
Image 7 earlier royal village: use ONLY ordinary paik uniform: navy jacket and trousers, white waistcloth and white headwrap, spear or sheathed sword. No timber-palace architecture.
Image 8 REAL Garhgaon Kareng Ghar photograph is the primary palace architecture reference: massive square stepped receding storeys, projecting cornices, decorated masonry pilasters, arched openings, compact top chamber. Do not replace this with Rang Ghar.

CRUCIAL CLEAN NEW PALACE:
Every visible palace wall, cornice, parapet and terrace is freshly finished in smooth warm ivory/cream lime plaster with subtle pale-ochre trim, finely defined new mouldings. Absolutely ZERO black patches, black mould, moss, soot, streaks, ageing, weather stains, cracks, exposed crumbling brick, ruined edges, dark patina. Natural shadows inside windows are fine; no dirty wall patches. It must look newly completed and dignified, not like present-day ruins. Preserve Kareng Ghar's stepped palace silhouette, no temple spires, minarets or Rang Ghar boat-roof. Fresh finish is an artistic reconstruction.

COMPOSITION TO KEEP ALL FACES READABLE:
A carefully staged single continuous scene, moderately wide rather than a distant establishing shot. Camera from a slightly elevated three-quarter position near the field, facing along the lowest usable palace terrace/balcony. The palace fills upper-left and background but its uppermost roofline may crop slightly to prioritise people. Use an open terrace on the existing stepped palace mass with a LOW solid clean masonry parapet, not an invented huge projecting European balcony. At the left upper-middle, Suteupha sits on a restrained carved wooden royal chair, torso and face fully visible above parapet. Ambika and Sarbeswari sit beside him, their faces clearly separated and near three-quarter frontal angle, watching the field. Keep the three royals prominent, not tiny distant faces hidden inside dark arches. THREE ordinary paiks stand behind/on terrace and two at field edge, never blocking faces.

Exactly TWO adult male Asian water buffalo in lower-centre/right field, broad muscular dark grey bodies, low heads, wide backswept curved horns locked together as they push against one another, four correct legs each, hooves planted, realistic anatomy. No cattle humps, no Spanish fighting bulls, no rider, no gore or injuries. Show both full bodies and connected horns clearly. Modest scuffed earth/short grass under them, very little airborne dust.
The THREE nasoni and TWO dhulia stand together at the far/right side of the field with a safe clear gap from the buffalo, in FRONT/THREE-QUARTER view so their faces and garments remain visible while their gazes turn toward the buffalo. Not a crowd seen only from behind. The featured reference-matching nasoni and dhulia are nearest to the camera, feet and drums visible. No cloned faces or extra duplicated royals. Keep composition uncluttered.

CLARITY:
Clean bright diffuse morning sunshine, natural light on ALL faces including royals on terrace, soft lifted shadows, high micro-detail in eyes, fabric weave and ornament; deep focus across people and buffalo, realistic scale and perspective, no fog, bloom, fake bokeh, painterly skin or orange haze. Crisp beautiful realistic Assam green vegetation and blue sky at field edge. No modern fencing, electric infrastructure, plastic, tourist signs, concrete landscaping, watermarks, decorative borders or collaged character-sheet panels. One coherent cinematic image.
